125	class AuditLog:
126	    """File-backed append-only audit log (one JSON object per line).
127	
128	    All appends are serialized by one process-wide lock plus an exclusive
129	    ``fcntl`` lock on a sidecar file, so multiple server threads and processes
130	    share a monotonic ``seq`` without interleaving or losing lines. Pagination
131	    cursors are HMAC-signed and bound to the tenant, the active filters and the
132	    ledger snapshot they were issued against.
133	    """
134	
135	    def __init__(self, data_dir: str) -> None:
136	        self.data_dir = data_dir
137	        os.makedirs(self.data_dir, exist_ok=True)
138	        self._log_path = os.path.join(data_dir, _LOG_NAME)
139	        self._lock_path = os.path.join(data_dir, _LOCK_NAME)
140	        self._secret_path = os.path.join(data_dir, _SECRET_NAME)
141	        self._append_lock = threading.Lock()
142	        self._secret: Optional[bytes] = None
143	
144	    # -- paths / locking ---------------------------------------------------
145	    @property
146	    def path(self) -> str:
147	        return self._log_path
148	
149	    def _locked_file(self):
150	        """Open the sidecar lock file and take an exclusive fcntl lock."""
151	        fd = os.open(self._lock_path, os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT, 0o600)
152	        if fcntl is None:  # pragma: no cover - non-POSIX platforms
153	            return fd
154	        try:
155	            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
156	        except OSError:
157	            os.close(fd)
158	            raise
159	        return fd
160	
161	    def _unlock_file(self, fd: int) -> None:
162	        try:
163	            if fcntl is not None:  # pragma: no branch - POSIX in practice
164	                fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
165	        finally:
166	            os.close(fd)
167	
168	    def _signing_secret(self) -> bytes:
169	        """Load (creating once, 0600) the HMAC secret used for cursors.
170	
171	        The read-or-create runs under the same cross-process file lock as
172	        appends, so two processes initializing concurrently cannot raise
173	        FileExistsError or read a half-written secret.
174	        """
175	        if self._secret is not None:
176	            return self._secret
177	        try:
178	            with open(self._secret_path, "rb") as fh:
179	                secret = fh.read()
180	            if secret:
181	                self._secret = secret
182	                return secret
183	        except FileNotFoundError:
184	            pass
185	        fd = self._locked_file()
186	        try:
187	            # Re-check under the lock: another process may have completed
188	            # the initialization while this one waited.
189	            try:
190	                with open(self._secret_path, "rb") as fh:
191	                    secret = fh.read()
192	                if secret:
193	                    self._secret = secret
194	                    return secret
195	            except FileNotFoundError:
196	                pass
197	            secret = os.urandom(32).hex().encode("ascii")
198	            out = os.open(
199	                self._secret_path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC, 0o600
200	            )
201	            try:
202	                os.write(out, secret)
203	                os.fsync(out)
204	            finally:
205	                os.close(out)
206	            self._secret = secret
207	            return secret
208	        finally:
209	            self._unlock_file(fd)
210	
211	    # -- reads -------------------------------------------------------------
212	    def _read_all_locked(self) -> List[AuditEvent]:
213	        """Read every ledger line. Caller must hold no lock; takes none."""
214	        try:
215	            with open(self._log_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
216	                lines = fh.readlines()
217	        except FileNotFoundError:
218	            return []
219	        except OSError as exc:
220	            raise LedgerError("cannot read audit log: %s" % exc) from exc
221	        events: List[AuditEvent] = []
222	        for line in lines:
223	            line = line.strip()
224	            if not line:
225	                continue
226	            try:
227	                events.append(AuditEvent.from_json(json.loads(line)))
228	            except (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError):
229	                # A torn/corrupt tail line must not poison reads; the writer
230	                # only ever fsyncs complete lines.
231	                continue
232	        return events
233	
234	    def _read_all(self) -> List[AuditEvent]:
235	        """Read under both locks for a consistent cross-process snapshot.
236	
237	        Appends commit (write + fsync) while holding the exclusive file
238	        lock, so a reader holding the same lock never observes a torn or
239	        partially-committed tail.
240	        """
241	        with self._append_lock:
242	            fd = self._locked_file()
243	            try:
244	                return self._read_all_locked()
245	            finally:
246	                self._unlock_file(fd)
247	
248	    @staticmethod
249	    def _fingerprint(events: List[AuditEvent]) -> str:
250	        """Stable digest identifying one ledger snapshot (its event set)."""
251	        digest = hashlib.sha256()
252	        for event in events:
253	            digest.update(str(event.seq).encode("ascii"))
254	            digest.update(b":")
255	            digest.update(event.event_id.encode("utf-8"))
256	            digest.update(b"\n")
257	        digest.update(b"count=%d" % len(events))
258	        return digest.hexdigest()
259	
260	    # -- writes ------------------------------------------------------------
261	    def new_event(
262	        self,
263	        tenant_id: Optional[str],
264	        action: str,
265	        key_id: Optional[str],
266	        outcome: str,
267	        timestamp: Optional[str] = None,
268	        event_id: Optional[str] = None,
269	    ) -> AuditEvent:
270	        """Mint an event with a fresh (or supplied) id and UTC timestamp.
271	
272	        ``event_id`` may be supplied so an idempotent operation's audit event
273	        is named after its ``operation_id``; crash recovery then resolves both
274	        by the same identifier. The ledger dedupes on event_id, so reusing an
275	        id never appends twice.
276	        """
277	        # Imported lazily to avoid a module import cycle at package import.
278	        from datetime import datetime, timezone
279	
280	        return AuditEvent(
281	            event_id=event_id or str(uuid.uuid4()),
282	            tenant_id=tenant_id,
283	            action=action,
284	            key_id=key_id,
285	            outcome=outcome,
286	            timestamp=timestamp
287	            or datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
288	        )
289	
290	    def append(self, event: AuditEvent) -> AuditEvent:
291	        """Append one event durably, assigning the next monotonic seq.
292	
293	        Raises LedgerError if the line cannot be committed. The fsync before
294	        release means a returned event is on disk.
295	        """
296	        with self._append_lock:
297	            fd = self._locked_file()
298	            try:
299	                existing = self._read_all_locked()
300	                # Idempotent on event_id: recovery re-append after a crash
301	                # between the ledger write and the outbox-marker clear must
302	                # not produce a duplicate line.
303	                for prior in existing:
304	                    if prior.event_id == event.event_id:
305	                        event.seq = prior.seq
306	                        return event
307	                event.seq = (existing[-1].seq + 1) if existing else 1
308	                line = json.dumps(event.to_json(), separators=(",", ":")) + "\n"
309	                try:
310	                    with open(self._log_path, "a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
311	                        fh.write(line)
312	                        fh.flush()
313	                        os.fsync(fh.fileno())
314	                except OSError as exc:
315	                    raise LedgerError("cannot write audit log: %s" % exc) from exc
316	            finally:
317	                self._unlock_file(fd)
318	        return event
319	
320	    def get_event(self, event_id: str) -> Optional[AuditEvent]:
321	        """Look up one event by event_id, or None if it has not been logged.
322	
323	        Used by multi-file restore recovery to decide whether the shared
324	        event reached the ledger after a crash.
325	        """
326	        for event in self._read_all():
327	            if event.event_id == event_id:
328	                return event
329	        return None
330	
331	    # -- cursors -----------------------------------------------------------
332	    def _encode_cursor(self, payload: dict) -> str:
333	        raw = json.dumps(payload, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True).encode("utf-8")
334	        token = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(raw).rstrip(b"=")
335	        mac = hmac.new(self._signing_secret(), token, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
336	        return (token + b"." + mac.encode("ascii")).decode("ascii")
337	
338	    def _decode_cursor(self, raw: str) -> dict:
339	        try:
340	            token_b, mac_b = raw.encode("ascii").split(b".", 1)
341	        except (ValueError, AttributeError) as exc:
342	            raise InvalidCursor("malformed cursor") from exc
343	        expected = hmac.new(
344	            self._signing_secret(), token_b, hashlib.sha256
345	        ).hexdigest().encode("ascii")
346	        if not hmac.compare_digest(expected, mac_b):
347	            raise InvalidCursor("invalid or tampered cursor")
348	        padded = token_b + b"=" * (-len(token_b) % 4)
349	        try:
350	            payload = json.loads(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(padded).decode("utf-8"))
351	        except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc:
352	            raise InvalidCursor("malformed cursor") from exc
353	        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
354	            raise InvalidCursor("malformed cursor")
355	        return payload
356	
357	    # -- queries -----------------------------------------------------------
358	    @staticmethod
359	    def _sort_key(event: AuditEvent):
360	        return event.timestamp, event.event_id, event.seq
361	
362	    def query(
363	        self,
364	        tenant_id: str,
365	        key_id: Optional[str] = None,
366	        action: Optional[str] = None,
367	        limit: int = 100,
368	        cursor: Optional[str] = None,
369	    ) -> AuditPage:
370	        """Return one tenant-isolated, filter-bound, snapshot-bound page.
371	
372	        Events are ordered by (timestamp, event_id) ascending. Conflict
373	        records carry a null tenant and are therefore visible to nobody.
374	        A cursor is valid only with the same tenant, filters and an unchanged
375	        ledger snapshot; otherwise InvalidCursor is raised.
376	        """
377	        anchor = None
378	        fingerprint = None
379	        if cursor is not None:
380	            payload = self._decode_cursor(cursor)
381	            try:
382	                if payload.get("t") != tenant_id:
383	                    raise InvalidCursor("cursor does not match tenant_id")
384	                if payload.get("k") != key_id or payload.get("a") != action:
385	                    raise InvalidCursor("cursor does not match filters")
386	                if int(payload.get("l", -1)) != limit:
387	                    raise InvalidCursor("cursor does not match limit")
388	                anchor = (payload["ts"], payload["eid"], int(payload["seq"]))
389	                fingerprint = payload["f"]
390	            except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
391	                raise InvalidCursor("malformed cursor") from exc
392	
393	        events = self._read_all()
394	
395	        selected_all = [
396	            e
397	            for e in events
398	            if e.tenant_id == tenant_id
399	            and (key_id is None or e.key_id == key_id)
400	            and (action is None or e.action == action)
401	        ]
402	        selected_all.sort(key=self._sort_key)
403	        # The snapshot is scoped to exactly the events this tenant and these
404	        # filters can see: another tenant's activity must not invalidate the
405	        # cursor, while any change to the visible set does.
406	        current_fingerprint = self._fingerprint(selected_all)
407	        if fingerprint is not None and fingerprint != current_fingerprint:
408	            raise InvalidCursor("cursor snapshot is no longer valid")
409	
410	        selected = selected_all
411	        if anchor is not None:
412	            selected = [e for e in selected if self._sort_key(e) > anchor]
413	
414	        page = selected[:limit]
415	        if len(selected) > limit and page:
416	            last = page[-1]
417	            next_cursor = self._encode_cursor(
418	                {
419	                    "v": 1,
420	                    "t": tenant_id,
421	                    "k": key_id,
422	                    "a": action,
423	                    "l": limit,
424	                    "ts": last.timestamp,
425	                    "eid": last.event_id,
426	                    "seq": last.seq,
427	                    "f": current_fingerprint,
428	                }
429	            )
430	        else:
431	            next_cursor = None
432	        return AuditPage(events=page, next_cursor=next_cursor)

@dataclass
class AuditEvent:
    """One immutable audit record. Never carries key material."""

    event_id: str
    tenant_id: Optional[str]
    action: str
    key_id: Optional[str]
    outcome: str
    timestamp: str
    seq: int = 0

    def to_json(self) -> dict:
        """Serialize to a plain dict suitable for JSON storage."""
        return {
            "event_id": self.event_id,
            "tenant_id": self.tenant_id,
            "action": self.action,
            "key_id": self.key_id,
            "outcome": self.outcome,
            "timestamp": self.timestamp,
            "seq": self.seq,
        }

    @classmethod
    def from_json(cls, data: dict) -> "AuditEvent":
        return cls(
            event_id=data["event_id"],
            tenant_id=data.get("tenant_id"),
            action=data["action"],
            key_id=data.get("key_id"),
            outcome=data["outcome"],
            timestamp=data["timestamp"],
            seq=int(data.get("seq", 0)),
        )

    def to_response(self) -> dict:
        """Projection for GET /v1/audit: ledger-internal seq is omitted."""
        return {
            "event_id": self.event_id,
            "tenant_id": self.tenant_id,
            "action": self.action,
            "key_id": self.key_id,
            "outcome": self.outcome,
            "timestamp": self.timestamp,
        }


class AuditPage(NamedTuple):
    """Result of one ledger query: a page of events and the next cursor."""

    events: List[AuditEvent]
    next_cursor: Optional[str]


class AuditLog:
    """File-backed append-only audit log (one JSON object per line).

    All appends are serialized by one process-wide lock plus an exclusive
    ``fcntl`` lock on a sidecar file, so multiple server threads and processes
    share a monotonic ``seq`` without interleaving or losing lines. Pagination
    cursors are HMAC-signed and bound to the tenant, the active filters and the
    ledger snapshot they were issued against.
    """

    def __init__(self, data_dir: str) -> None:
        self.data_dir = data_dir
        os.makedirs(self.data_dir, exist_ok=True)
        self._log_path = os.path.join(data_dir, _LOG_NAME)
        self._lock_path = os.path.join(data_dir, _LOCK_NAME)
        self._secret_path = os.path.join(data_dir, _SECRET_NAME)
        self._append_lock = threading.Lock()
        self._secret: Optional[bytes] = None

    # -- paths / locking ---------------------------------------------------
    @property
    def path(self) -> str:
        return self._log_path

    def _locked_file(self):
        """Open the sidecar lock file and take an exclusive fcntl lock."""
        fd = os.open(self._lock_path, os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT, 0o600)
        if fcntl is None:  # pragma: no cover - non-POSIX platforms
            return fd
        try:
            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
        except OSError:
            os.close(fd)
            raise
        return fd

    def _unlock_file(self, fd: int) -> None:
        try:
            if fcntl is not None:  # pragma: no branch - POSIX in practice
                fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
        finally:
            os.close(fd)

    def _signing_secret(self) -> bytes:
        """Load (creating once, 0600) the HMAC secret used for cursors.

        The read-or-create runs under the same cross-process file lock as
        appends, so two processes initializing concurrently cannot raise
        FileExistsError or read a half-written secret.
        """
        if self._secret is not None:
            return self._secret
        try:
            with open(self._secret_path, "rb") as fh:
                secret = fh.read()
            if secret:
                self._secret = secret
                return secret
        except FileNotFoundError:
            pass
        fd = self._locked_file()
        try:
            # Re-check under the lock: another process may have completed
            # the initialization while this one waited.
            try:
                with open(self._secret_path, "rb") as fh:
                    secret = fh.read()
                if secret:
                    self._secret = secret
                    return secret
            except FileNotFoundError:
                pass
            secret = os.urandom(32).hex().encode("ascii")
            out = os.open(
                self._secret_path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC, 0o600
            )
            try:
                os.write(out, secret)
                os.fsync(out)
            finally:
                os.close(out)
            self._secret = secret
            return secret
        finally:
            self._unlock_file(fd)

    # -- reads -------------------------------------------------------------
    def _read_all_locked(self) -> List[AuditEvent]:
        """Read every ledger line. Caller must hold no lock; takes none."""
        try:
            with open(self._log_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
                lines = fh.readlines()
        except FileNotFoundError:
            return []
        except OSError as exc:
            raise LedgerError("cannot read audit log: %s" % exc) from exc
        events: List[AuditEvent] = []
        for line in lines:
            line = line.strip()
            if not line:
                continue
            try:
                events.append(AuditEvent.from_json(json.loads(line)))
            except (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError):
                # A torn/corrupt tail line must not poison reads; the writer
                # only ever fsyncs complete lines.
                continue
        return events

    def _read_all(self) -> List[AuditEvent]:
        """Read under both locks for a consistent cross-process snapshot.

        Appends commit (write + fsync) while holding the exclusive file
        lock, so a reader holding the same lock never observes a torn or
        partially-committed tail.
        """
        with self._append_lock:
            fd = self._locked_file()
            try:
                return self._read_all_locked()
            finally:
                self._unlock_file(fd)

    @staticmethod
    def _fingerprint(events: List[AuditEvent]) -> str:
        """Stable digest identifying one ledger snapshot (its event set)."""
        digest = hashlib.sha256()
        for event in events:
            digest.update(str(event.seq).encode("ascii"))
            digest.update(b":")
            digest.update(event.event_id.encode("utf-8"))
            digest.update(b"\n")
        digest.update(b"count=%d" % len(events))
        return digest.hexdigest()

    # -- writes ------------------------------------------------------------
    def new_event(
        self,
        tenant_id: Optional[str],
        action: str,
        key_id: Optional[str],
        outcome: str,
        timestamp: Optional[str] = None,
        event_id: Optional[str] = None,
    ) -> AuditEvent:
        """Mint an event with a fresh (or supplied) id and UTC timestamp.

        ``event_id`` may be supplied so an idempotent operation's audit event
        is named after its ``operation_id``; crash recovery then resolves both
        by the same identifier. The ledger dedupes on event_id, so reusing an
        id never appends twice.
        """
        # Imported lazily to avoid a module import cycle at package import.
        from datetime import datetime, timezone

        return AuditEvent(
            event_id=event_id or str(uuid.uuid4()),
            tenant_id=tenant_id,
            action=action,
            key_id=key_id,
            outcome=outcome,
            timestamp=timestamp
            or datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        )

    def append(self, event: AuditEvent) -> AuditEvent:
        """Append one event durably, assigning the next monotonic seq.

        Raises LedgerError if the line cannot be committed. The fsync before
        release means a returned event is on disk.
        """
        with self._append_lock:
            fd = self._locked_file()
            try:
                existing = self._read_all_locked()
                # Idempotent on event_id: recovery re-append after a crash
                # between the ledger write and the outbox-marker clear must
                # not produce a duplicate line.
                for prior in existing:
                    if prior.event_id == event.event_id:
                        event.seq = prior.seq
                        return event
                event.seq = (existing[-1].seq + 1) if existing else 1
                line = json.dumps(event.to_json(), separators=(",", ":")) + "\n"
                try:
                    with open(self._log_path, "a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
                        fh.write(line)
                        fh.flush()
                        os.fsync(fh.fileno())
                except OSError as exc:
                    raise LedgerError("cannot write audit log: %s" % exc) from exc
            finally:
                self._unlock_file(fd)
        return event

    def get_event(self, event_id: str) -> Optional[AuditEvent]:
        """Look up one event by event_id, or None if it has not been logged.

        Used by multi-file restore recovery to decide whether the shared
        event reached the ledger after a crash.
        """
        for event in self._read_all():
            if event.event_id == event_id:
                return event
        return None

    # -- cursors -----------------------------------------------------------
    def _encode_cursor(self, payload: dict) -> str:
        raw = json.dumps(payload, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True).encode("utf-8")
        token = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(raw).rstrip(b"=")
        mac = hmac.new(self._signing_secret(), token, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
        return (token + b"." + mac.encode("ascii")).decode("ascii")

    def _decode_cursor(self, raw: str) -> dict:
        try:
            token_b, mac_b = raw.encode("ascii").split(b".", 1)
        except (ValueError, AttributeError) as exc:
            raise InvalidCursor("malformed cursor") from exc
        expected = hmac.new(
            self._signing_secret(), token_b, hashlib.sha256
        ).hexdigest().encode("ascii")
        if not hmac.compare_digest(expected, mac_b):
            raise InvalidCursor("invalid or tampered cursor")
        padded = token_b + b"=" * (-len(token_b) % 4)
        try:
            payload = json.loads(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(padded).decode("utf-8"))
        except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc:
            raise InvalidCursor("malformed cursor") from exc
        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
            raise InvalidCursor("malformed cursor")
        return payload

    # -- queries -----------------------------------------------------------
    @staticmethod
    def _sort_key(event: AuditEvent):
        return event.timestamp, event.event_id, event.seq

    def query(
        self,
        tenant_id: str,
        key_id: Optional[str] = None,
        action: Optional[str] = None,
        limit: int = 100,
        cursor: Optional[str] = None,
    ) -> AuditPage:
        """Return one tenant-isolated, filter-bound, snapshot-bound page.

        Events are ordered by (timestamp, event_id) ascending. Conflict
        records carry a null tenant and are therefore visible to nobody.
        A cursor is valid only with the same tenant, filters and an unchanged
        ledger snapshot; otherwise InvalidCursor is raised.
        """
        anchor = None
        fingerprint = None
        if cursor is not None:
            payload = self._decode_cursor(cursor)
            try:
                if payload.get("t") != tenant_id:
                    raise InvalidCursor("cursor does not match tenant_id")
                if payload.get("k") != key_id or payload.get("a") != action:
                    raise InvalidCursor("cursor does not match filters")
                if int(payload.get("l", -1)) != limit:
                    raise InvalidCursor("cursor does not match limit")
                anchor = (payload["ts"], payload["eid"], int(payload["seq"]))
                fingerprint = payload["f"]
            except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
                raise InvalidCursor("malformed cursor") from exc

        events = self._read_all()

        selected_all = [
            e
            for e in events
            if e.tenant_id == tenant_id
            and (key_id is None or e.key_id == key_id)
            and (action is None or e.action == action)
        ]
        selected_all.sort(key=self._sort_key)
        # The snapshot is scoped to exactly the events this tenant and these
        # filters can see: another tenant's activity must not invalidate the
        # cursor, while any change to the visible set does.
        current_fingerprint = self._fingerprint(selected_all)
        if fingerprint is not None and fingerprint != current_fingerprint:
            raise InvalidCursor("cursor snapshot is no longer valid")

        selected = selected_all
        if anchor is not None:
            selected = [e for e in selected if self._sort_key(e) > anchor]

        page = selected[:limit]
        if len(selected) > limit and page:
            last = page[-1]
            next_cursor = self._encode_cursor(
                {
                    "v": 1,
                    "t": tenant_id,
                    "k": key_id,
                    "a": action,
                    "l": limit,
                    "ts": last.timestamp,
                    "eid": last.event_id,
                    "seq": last.seq,
                    "f": current_fingerprint,
                }
            )
        else:
            next_cursor = None
        return AuditPage(events=page, next_cursor=next_cursor)

4	durable) and before any KMS/HSM provider is called, the rotate / import /
5	restore / batch-rotate executors create one mirror file
6	``operation-artifacts/<operation_id>.json`` (0600, fsynced, atomic rename).
7	
8	The mirror is the single crash-recovery cross-reference tying together every
9	durable artifact of one attempt:
10	
11	* the idempotent operation record ``operations/<operation_id>.json``;
12	* the provider provision journal ``provisions/<operation_id>.json`` and every
13	  freshly minted handle (``provider_id``/``handle``);
14	* a restore's write set and shared marker (``_restore`` / ``_empty``);

394	        i.e. the provider was never effectively called. Anything less provable
395	        raises ArtifactStrandUnavailable: the operation stays pending, the
396	        scene stays parked for the next process restart, and no provider is
397	        called twice.
398	        """
399	        operation_id = operation.operation_id
400	        return self._Attempt(
401	            self, operation, operation_id, blocking, takeover,
402	            operation_store,
403	        )

405	    class _Attempt:
406	        def __init__(self, store, operation, operation_id, blocking,
407	                     takeover, operation_store):
408	            self.store = store
409	            self.operation = operation
410	            self.operation_id = operation_id
411	            self.blocking = blocking
412	            self.takeover = takeover
413	            self.operation_store = operation_store
414	            self._cm = None
415	            self.mirror = None
416	
417	        def __enter__(self):
418	            self._cm = self.store._claim(
419	                self.operation_id, self.blocking
420	            )
421	            self._cm.__enter__()
422	            try:
423	                self.mirror = self.store._claim_strand(
424	                    self.operation, self.takeover, self.operation_store
425	                )
426	                return self.mirror
427	            except BaseException:
428	                self._cm.__exit__(None, None, None)
429	                self._cm = None
430	                raise
431	
432	        def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc, tb):
433	            try:
434	                return None
435	            finally:
436	                if self._cm is not None:
437	                    self._cm.__exit__(exc_type, exc, tb)

439	    def write_descriptor(self, descriptor: dict) -> None:
440	        """Atomically write one mirror (0600, fsynced before rename)."""
441	        path = self.path_for(descriptor["operation_id"])
442	        fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=self.dir_path, suffix=".tmp")
443	        try:
444	            with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
445	                json.dump(descriptor, fh)
446	                fh.flush()
447	                os.fsync(fh.fileno())
448	            os.chmod(tmp_path, 0o600)
449	            os.replace(tmp_path, path)
450	        except BaseException:
451	            try:
452	                os.unlink(tmp_path)
453	            except OSError:
454	                pass
455	            raise

457	    def _read_descriptor(self, operation_id: str) -> Optional[dict]:
458	        try:
459	            with open(self.path_for(operation_id), "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
460	                data = json.load(fh)
461	        except (OSError, ValueError):
462	            return None
463	        if not isinstance(data, dict):
464	            return None
465	        return data

467	    def discard(self, operation_id: str) -> bool:
468	        try:
469	            os.unlink(self.path_for(operation_id))
470	            return True
471	        except FileNotFoundError:
472	            return True
473	        except OSError:
474	            return False

476	    def is_parked(self, operation_id: str) -> bool:
477	        """Whether a pending operation must be kept pending at settlement.
478	
479	        Both genuinely parked evidence sets (corrupt/inconsistent, provider
480	        down) and clean pre-provider strands waiting for a takeover retry keep
481	        the operation pending: neither may be finalized failed(500), so the
482	        request path is the only thing allowed to conclude them.
483	        """
484	        return operation_id in self._parked

486	    # -- request-path strand claim / takeover ------------------------------
487	    def _event_durable(self, operation_id: str):
488	        """Return the durable event for the id, or None; False if unreadable."""
489	        try:
490	            return self.audit.get_event(operation_id)
491	        except LedgerError:
492	            return False

494	    def _clean_strand_descriptor(self, operation, descriptor: dict) -> bool:
495	        """Whether the attempt provably never reached a provider.
496	
497	        Evidence required to (re)start a bound attempt under the same
498	        operation_id: no durable event of any outcome, no provision journal,
499	        no batch snapshot, no restore marker and no key/policy pending marker
500	        naming this operation. Anything less returns False and the caller
501	        parks instead of guessing.
502	        """
503	        if self.key_store is None:
504	            return False
505	        event = self._event_durable(operation.operation_id)
506	        if event is False or event is not None:
507	            # Unreadable ledger, or a durable commit/rejection: the startup
508	            # settlement owns those; a request never re-runs them.
509	            return False
510	        return not self._residual_evidence(descriptor)

512	    def _claim_strand(self, operation, takeover: bool,
513	                      operation_store=None) -> ArtifactMirror:
514	        """Create (fresh bind) or safely take over the attempt mirror.
515	
516	        Claim lock is held. A fresh bind never had an attempt, so its mirror
517	        is created directly WITHOUT reading the ledger (a get_event there
518	        would block behind a held audit lock before the first provider call).
519	        Only an explicit takeover re-reads the operation record (the claim is
520	        the serialization boundary with the original owner) and re-validates
521	        the surviving evidence.
522	        """
523	        if not takeover:
524	            try:
525	                return self.create(operation)
526	            except OSError as exc:
527	                raise ArtifactStrandUnavailable(str(exc), 500)
528	        operation_id = operation.operation_id
529	        # Re-read the record UNDER the claim: the original owner may have
530	        # reached a terminal after this request observed "pending" but before
531	        # the claim was granted. Hand the fresh terminal to the caller for an
532	        # exact replay rather than re-executing or wrongly parking it.
533	        if operation_store is not None:
534	            fresh = operation_store._read_record(operation_id)
535	            if fresh is not None and fresh.is_terminal():
536	                raise ArtifactAlreadyTerminal(fresh)
537	        descriptor = self._read_descriptor(operation_id)
538	        if descriptor is not None:
539	            if not self._binding_matches(descriptor, operation):
540	                raise ArtifactStrandUnavailable(
541	                    "mirror does not match the operation binding"
542	                )
543	            return self._take_over(operation, descriptor)
544	        if os.path.exists(self.path_for(operation_id)):
545	            # Named on disk but unparseable: a corrupt mirror is evidence to
546	            # preserve, never rebuilt over by a live request.
547	            raise ArtifactStrandUnavailable("corrupt mirror")
548	        # Missing mirror: the classic failed strand (mirror creation raised
549	        # before the first provider call) -- only restartable when not a trace
550	        # of the attempt survives and nothing committed under this id.
551	        probe = {
552	            "operation_id": operation_id,
553	            "journal": None,
554	            "snapshot": None,
555	            "empty_marker": None,
556	        }
557	        if not self._clean_strand_descriptor(operation, probe):
558	            raise ArtifactStrandUnavailable(
559	                "missing mirror with surviving or uncertain evidence"
560	            )
561	        try:
562	            return self.create(operation)
563	        except OSError as exc:
564	            raise ArtifactStrandUnavailable(str(exc), 500)

566	    def _take_over(
567	        self, operation, descriptor: dict
568	    ) -> ArtifactMirror:
569	        """Re-open an intact, never-committed mirror for a retried attempt.
570	
571	        Only a mirror that provably never reached a provider can be restarted
572	        on the request path: it is still at the ``bound`` phase with no handle
573	        recorded, has no provision journal/batch snapshot/marker and has no
574	        durable event of any outcome. A mirror that reached provisioning (a
575	        journal or a handle existed) is finalized by the startup crash rule
576	        instead -- a request never re-executes it. The descriptor is reset to
577	        a fresh ``bound`` image as the executor re-describes the write set.
578	        """
579	        phase = descriptor.get("phase")
580	        if phase != PHASE_BOUND or descriptor.get("handles"):
581	            raise ArtifactStrandUnavailable(
582	                "mirror phase %r cannot be taken over" % phase
583	            )
584	        if descriptor.get("journal") or descriptor.get("snapshot"):
585	            raise ArtifactStrandUnavailable(
586	                "mirror already references a journal or snapshot"
587	            )
588	        if not self._clean_strand_descriptor(operation, descriptor):
589	            raise ArtifactStrandUnavailable(
590	                "surviving evidence blocks the mirror takeover"
591	            )
592	        # Reset the durable image to a fresh bound strand. Discard first so a
593	        # stale reference can never ride along.
594	        if not self.discard(operation.operation_id):
595	            raise ArtifactStrandUnavailable("stale mirror could not be removed")
596	        try:
597	            return self.create(operation)
598	        except OSError as exc:
599	            raise ArtifactStrandUnavailable(str(exc), 500)

601	    # -- request-path lifecycle -------------------------------------------
602	    def create(self, operation) -> ArtifactMirror:
603	        """Create the bound-phase mirror for a freshly bound operation.
604	
605	        The mirror only carries the binding facts (tenant, operator, path,
606	        canonical request) and the ``bound`` phase; the executor adds kind,
607	        action and write set (still before the first provider call).
608	        """
609	        descriptor = {
610	            "version": 1,
611	            "operation_id": operation.operation_id,
612	            "tenant_id": operation.tenant_id,
613	            "operator_id": operation.operator_id,
614	            "path": operation.path,
615	            "request_body": operation.request_body,
616	            "kind": None,
617	            "action": None,
618	            "phase": PHASE_BOUND,
619	            "write_set": [],
620	            "handles": [],
621	            "journal": None,
622	            "snapshot": None,
623	            "empty_marker": None,
624	            "policy": False,
625	            "created_at": _new_timestamp(),
626	            "updated_at": None,
627	        }
628	        os.makedirs(self.dir_path, exist_ok=True)
629	        self.write_descriptor(descriptor)
630	        return ArtifactMirror(self, operation, descriptor)

632	    def after_terminal(self, mirror: Optional[ArtifactMirror]) -> None:
633	        """Request-path mirror cleanup once an attempt ran.
634	
635	        Committed terminals verify ownership of every minted handle; refusal/
636	        failure terminals require the attempt's rollback artifacts to be gone.
637	        A mirror whose evidence cannot be verified (a delete the provider
638	        could not confirm, an unreadable ledger) is intentionally LEFT on
639	        disk: the next startup settles it, and until then the evidence stays
640	        complete.
641	
642	        A still-``bound`` mirror whose operation is PENDING (the describe/
643	        provision step itself failed before a provider was called) is retained
644	        too: the mirror stays the parked attempt's cross-reference until a
645	        same-id HTTP/CLI retry takes it over. Only a mirror whose operation
646	        actually reached a terminal is eligible for the bound-phase discard.
647	        """
648	        if mirror is None:
649	            return
650	        descriptor = self._read_descriptor(mirror.operation_id)
651	        if descriptor is None:
652	            return
653	        phase = descriptor.get("phase")
654	        if phase == PHASE_COMMITTED:
655	            if self._committed_state_verified(descriptor):
656	                self.discard(mirror.operation_id)
657	            return
658	        if phase == PHASE_BOUND:
659	            # A rejection/provider terminal finalizes the operation and clears
660	            # an untouched bound mirror; a strand failure leaves it pending and
661	            # keeps the mirror as the parked attempt's index.
662	            if getattr(mirror.operation, "status", None) == "pending":
663	                return
664	            if not self._residual_evidence(descriptor):
665	                self.discard(mirror.operation_id)
666	            return
667	        if phase == PHASE_ROLLED_BACK:
668	            if not self._residual_evidence(descriptor):
669	                self.discard(mirror.operation_id)
670	            return
671	        # provisioning/staged after a terminal response: the store's abort
672	        # path either verified the rollback (journal/snapshot gone) or parked
673	        # the scene. Decide from the durable facts, never from the phase.
674	        if not self._residual_evidence(descriptor):
675	            self.discard(mirror.operation_id)

677	    # -- startup settlement ------------------------------------------------
678	    def settle_pending(self, operation_store) -> None:
679	        """Settle surviving mirrors of crashed processes at startup.
680	
681	        Must run AFTER the key-store and restore outbox recovery (which settle
682	        files, markers, snapshots, journals and handles) and BEFORE the
683	        operation store finalizes pending operations. A mirror whose commit
684	        event is durable and consistent is discarded; a mirror of a fully
685	        rolled-back attempt is discarded (the operation then finalizes as the
686	        stored 500 interruption); anything unprovable keeps the ENTIRE
687	        evidence set and parks the operation pending for a later open.
688	        """
689	        self._parked = set()
690	        try:
691	            names = os.listdir(self.dir_path)
692	        except OSError:
693	            # The mirror directory itself is unreadable: settle nothing and
694	            # let the missing-mirror pass below park every bound operation
695	            # rather than finalizing one without its evidence.
696	            names = []
697	        for name in names:
698	            if not name.endswith(".json"):
699	                continue
700	            operation_id = name[:-5]
701	            if not _is_uuid4(operation_id):
702	                # An unidentifiable mirror can never be cross-checked against
703	                # an operation/event: keep it for operator resolution.
704	                continue
705	            self._settle_one(operation_id, operation_store)
706	        self._settle_missing_mirrors(names, operation_store)
707	
708	    def _settle_missing_mirrors(self, mirror_names, operation_store) -> None:
709	        """Park pending operations of the mirrored generation with no mirror.
710	
711	        A ``mirror_required`` pending operation whose mirror never landed (the
712	        0600 creation failed, or the process died on that exact syscall) is not
713	        guessed into failed(500): with no evidence it stays pending as a clean
714	        strand the next identical HTTP/CLI request takes over under the same
715	        operation_id; with surviving evidence it is parked the same way until
716	        a later open. Records predating mirrors (``mirror_required`` false)
717	        keep the legacy recovery rules and are intentionally untouched.
718	        """
719	        present = {name[:-5] for name in mirror_names if name.endswith(".json")}
720	        try:
721	            op_names = os.listdir(operation_store.dir_path)
722	        except OSError:
723	            return
724	        for name in op_names:
725	            if not name.endswith(".json") or name == "index.json":
726	                continue
727	            operation_id = name[:-5]
728	            if operation_id in present:
729	                continue
730	            record = operation_store._read_record(operation_id)
731	            if record is None or record.is_terminal():
732	                continue
733	            if not getattr(record, "mirror_required", False):
734	                # Legacy binding: no mirror was ever mandatory.
735	                continue
736	            self._parked.add(operation_id)
737	
738	    def _settle_one(self, operation_id: str, operation_store) -> None:
739	        descriptor = self._read_descriptor(operation_id)
740	        if descriptor is None:
741	            # Corrupt/unreadable mirror: preserve the evidence and park the
742	            # operation rather than guessing.
743	            self._parked.add(operation_id)
744	            return
745	        record = operation_store._read_record(operation_id)
746	        if record is None or not self._binding_matches(descriptor, record):
747	            # Mirror references a missing operation or a different binding:
748	            # the two durable records disagree, nothing can be guessed.
749	            self._parked.add(operation_id)
750	            return
751	        try:
752	            event = self.audit.get_event(operation_id)
753	        except LedgerError:
754	            # The commit authority cannot be read: retain everything.
755	            self._parked.add(operation_id)
756	            return
757	
758	        if record.is_terminal():
759	            # The original process reached a terminal before dying; only the
760	            # mirror unlink may have been missed. Never re-finalize it.
761	            self._settle_terminal(descriptor, record, event)
762	            return
763	
764	        # Pending operation.
765	        if event is not None and self._event_confirms(descriptor, event):
766	            # Durable success with matching action/tenant. Keep the new
767	            # versions and clean the mirror ONLY once the committed write set,
768	            # every surviving reference and the staged 201 response all verify.
769	            # The event is the commit fact regardless of residual markers, so a
770	            # verification miss parks the evidence but never rolls it back.
771	            if self._committed_state_verified(descriptor) and (
772	                self._staged_success_response_backed(descriptor, record)
773	            ):
774	                self.discard(operation_id)
775	            return
776	        if event is not None and event.outcome == audit_mod.OUTCOME_SUCCESS:
777	            # A durable success carries this id but action/tenant disagree:
778	            # an id collision. Neither commit nor rollback is provable.
779	            self._parked.add(operation_id)
780	            return
781	        if event is not None and not self._rejected_event_matches(
782	            descriptor, record, event
783	        ):
784	            # A durable event with this id is not the mirror's own rejection
785	            # (action/tenant/key/outcome or staged response mismatch): the id
786	            # collides with a different terminal. Park rather than replaying.
787	            self._parked.add(operation_id)
788	            return
789	        # Event absent, or a durable rejected terminal that matches: the
790	        # attempt never committed its write set. The outbox recovery has
791	        # either finished the rollback or deliberately parked the scene
792	        # (provider down, corrupt/missing basis).
793	        if self._residual_evidence(descriptor):
794	            self._parked.add(operation_id)
795	            return
796	        if event is not None:
797	            # A durable, matching rejected terminal (403/404/409/503) with no
798	            # residual file/journal: the rejection already committed and the
799	            # operation store replays its staged result verbatim; the mirror
800	            # is spent housekeeping. Never park a decided terminal for a retry.
801	            self.discard(operation_id)
802	            return
803	        # No event and no residual evidence. Decide from whether the provider
804	        # was ever reached: a mirror that stayed at ``bound`` (no journal/
805	        # handle) represents an attempt interrupted exactly around mirror
806	        # creation -- keep it pending (and retain the mirror as its index) so
807	        # the next identical HTTP/CLI request takes it over under the same
808	        # operation_id. A mirror that reached provisioning and was then fully
809	        # rolled back (provider failure / conflict / ledger failure) is the
810	        # legacy interruption: drop the mirror so the operation finalizes
811	        # failed(500) exactly as before.
812	        if self._never_provisioned(descriptor):
813	            self._parked.add(operation_id)
814	        else:
815	            self.discard(operation_id)
816	
817	    @staticmethod
818	    def _never_provisioned(descriptor: dict) -> bool:
819	        """Whether the mirror proves the provider was never reached."""
820	        return (
821	            descriptor.get("phase") == PHASE_BOUND
822	            and not descriptor.get("handles")
823	            and not descriptor.get("journal")
824	            and not descriptor.get("snapshot")
825	        )

827	    def _settle_terminal(self, descriptor: dict, record, event) -> None:
828	        """Discard a terminal operation's mirror only when its state verifies."""
829	        if record.status == "succeeded":
830	            if event is not None and self._event_confirms(descriptor, event):
831	                if self._committed_state_verified(
832	                    descriptor
833	                ) and self._staged_success_response_backed(descriptor, record):
834	                    self.discard(record.operation_id)
835	            return
836	        # failed/conflict/timed_out: an uncommitted terminal. A durable
837	        # rejection must still BE this mirror's rejection (action/tenant/
838	        # outcome/response agree); the store/restore recovery removes the
839	        # artifacts, so a surviving journal/snapshot/marker means cleanup is
840	        # still retrying and the mirror stays as its index.
841	        if event is not None and not self._rejected_event_matches(
842	            descriptor, record, event
843	        ):
844	            return
845	        if not self._residual_evidence(descriptor):
846	            self.discard(record.operation_id)

848	    # -- verification primitives -------------------------------------------
849	    @staticmethod
850	    def _descriptor_consistent(descriptor: dict, allow_undescribed: bool):
851	        """Whether one on-disk mirror descriptor is internally well-formed.
852	
853	        A descriptor is the cross-index of an attempt, so every reference it
854	        carries must already be self-consistent before it is compared against
855	        anything else:
856	
857	        * ``kind`` (once described) is one of the four mirrored mutations and
858	          ``action`` is exactly the audit action that kind commits with;
859	        * ``write_set`` is a list of unique canonical key ids with the kind's
860	          exact shape (rotate/import one key; batch a non-empty set; restore a
861	          possibly empty set);
862	        * ``handles`` is a duplicate-free list of non-empty
863	          ``{provider_id, handle}`` pairs;
864	        * the journal/snapshot references name the operation itself and a
865	          snapshot only accompanies a batch rotation.
866	
867	        ``allow_undescribed`` admits a still-``bound`` mirror that crashed
868	        before ``describe`` (kind/action unset, empty write set).
869	        """
870	        if not isinstance(descriptor, dict):
871	            return False
872	        operation_id = descriptor.get("operation_id")
873	        if not _is_uuid4(operation_id):
874	            return False
875	        for field in ("tenant_id", "operator_id", "path", "request_body"):
876	            value = descriptor.get(field)
877	            if not isinstance(value, str):
878	                return False
879	        if not descriptor.get("tenant_id"):
880	            return False
881	        kind = descriptor.get("kind")
882	        action = descriptor.get("action")
883	        write_set = descriptor.get("write_set")
884	        if kind is None:
885	            if not allow_undescribed:
886	                return False
887	            if action is not None or write_set:
888	                return False
889	        else:
890	            if kind not in _KIND_ACTIONS or action != _KIND_ACTIONS[kind]:
891	                return False
892	            if not ArtifactStore._valid_write_set_shape(kind, write_set):
893	                return False
894	        journal = descriptor.get("journal")
895	        if journal is not None and journal != operation_id:
896	            return False
897	        snapshot = descriptor.get("snapshot")
898	        if snapshot is not None:
899	            if snapshot != operation_id or kind != "batch_rotate":
900	                return False
901	        empty_marker = descriptor.get("empty_marker")
902	        if empty_marker is not None and not isinstance(empty_marker, str):
903	            return False
904	        if not isinstance(descriptor.get("policy"), bool):
905	            return False
906	        handles = descriptor.get("handles")
907	        if not isinstance(handles, list):
908	            return False
909	        seen = set()
910	        for entry in handles:
911	            if not isinstance(entry, dict):
912	                return False
913	            provider_id = entry.get("provider_id")
914	            handle = entry.get("handle")
915	            if (
916	                not isinstance(provider_id, str)
917	                or not provider_id
918	                or not isinstance(handle, str)
919	                or not handle
920	            ):
921	                return False
922	            pair = (provider_id, handle)
923	            if pair in seen:
924	                return False
925	            seen.add(pair)
926	        return True
927	
928	    @staticmethod
929	    def _valid_write_set_shape(kind: str, write_set) -> bool:
930	        """The kind's exact write-set shape (unique canonical UUID4s)."""
931	        if not isinstance(write_set, list):
932	            return False
933	        seen = set()
934	        for key_id in write_set:
935	            if not _is_key_id(key_id) or key_id in seen:
936	                return False
937	            seen.add(key_id)
938	        if kind in ("rotate", "import") and len(seen) != 1:
939	            return False
940	        if kind == "batch_rotate" and not seen:
941	            return False
942	        return True
943	
944	    @staticmethod
945	    def _details_correspond(descriptor: dict, record) -> bool:
946	        """Whether the operation record's durable details match the mirror.
947	
948	        The kind/action must correspond to the exact ``key_id`` (rotate/
949	        import), ``items`` set (batch rotation) or ``key_ids`` plus policy
950	        flag (restore) the executor persisted in ``operations/<id>.json``.
951	        A mirror that was never described has nothing yet to correspond.
952	        """
953	        kind = descriptor.get("kind")
954	        if kind is None:
955	            return True
956	        details = getattr(record, "details", None)
957	        if not isinstance(details, dict) or details.get("kind") != kind:
958	            return False
959	        write_set = descriptor.get("write_set") or []
960	        if kind in ("rotate", "import"):
961	            return details.get("key_id") == (write_set[0] if write_set else None)
962	        if kind == "batch_rotate":
963	            items = details.get("items")
964	            if not isinstance(items, list):
965	                return False
966	            item_keys = set()
967	            for item in items:
968	                if not isinstance(item, dict) or not _is_key_id(
969	                    item.get("key_id")
970	                ):
971	                    return False
972	                item_keys.add(item["key_id"])

1286	        if not os.path.exists(path):

1288	        try:
1289	            with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:

1299	                line = json.loads(raw)
1300	            except ValueError:

1302	            if not isinstance(line, dict):

1305	                )
1306	            if index == 0 and "operation_id" in line:

1309	            provider_id = line.get("provider_id")
1310	            handle = line.get("handle")

1324	                )
